target_customer: Product designers and design-minded developers at startups who want to edit a real React and Next.js codebase visually instead of handing off mockups
problem: Designers work in mockup tools and hand off to engineers, so the shipped product drifts from the design. Onlook lets designers change the real code through a visual canvas and AI.
business_model: Open source (Apache 2.0) editor, free to self-host; hosted cloud version sold by contacting the team
product_category: Open-source visual editor for code (design to code, AI developer tool)

founders.name: Daniel Farrell
previous_startups: Wanderlift (long-distance ridesharing, co-founder, outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: YC page: professional designer for over a decade, first 100 employees at Bird on global expansion strategy, later Head of Growth at DIMO. Education not stated.

founders.name: Kiet Ho
founders.background_notes: YC page: engineer at Amazon and ServiceNow who worked directly with designers; started the company in January 2024. Education not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mapping edits on a rendered page back to React and Tailwind source code and keeping the two in sync is hard for a four person team, but it builds on existing frameworks and LLM APIs rather than research.

defensibility.rationale: The code is open source under Apache 2.0, so anyone can fork it (several forks appear on GitHub). The advantage is community size and early mindshare, with over 26,000 GitHub stars per the company site.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Prompt-to-app tools and site builders were already shipping when Onlook launched in early 2025. Third-party comparisons describe v0 and Bolt as generating new code while Onlook edits existing code. No source found showing an incumbent copying the exact wedge.

market_need_then: Design-to-code handoff friction was a known complaint, and AI code editors such as Cursor had just created demand for designers to work in code. Launch traction (number one on Hacker News and twice the number one trending GitHub repo per the YC page) shows interest.

branding.community_and_virality: Number one on Hacker News and twice the number one trending GitHub repo per the YC company page; over 26,000 GitHub stars per the company site; open source contributors worldwide per the FAQ.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear positioning line and strong open source launch buzz, but no mascot or distinctive identity found in sources.

outcome_analysis: Onlook is active and had no reported exit, shutdown or layoffs in searches. It rode the AI code editor wave with an open source launch that reached the top of Hacker News and GitHub trending, and it built a large star count quickly. Funding is thin in verified sources, with only aggregator figures, so the commercial outcome is unproven. The main risks are forks and well-funded prompt-to-app tools.
